title: Series length 1 doesn't match DataFrame height 3 in `select()`
body: I am reopening the earlier issue because the same serialized lazy query plan still fails on Polars 1.8.1. Collecting the three-row plan raises `Series: line, length 1 doesn't match the DataFrame height of 3` and suggests adding `.first()` so the Series can be broadcast.

symptoms_visible: Collecting the serialized three-row lazy plan in Polars 1.8.1 raises `Series: line, length 1 doesn't match the DataFrame height of 3` and suggests adding `.first()`.
N0.label: N0 length mismatch reported

symptoms_visible: The query completes locally but fails every time in the Read the Docs runner, and the exception appears only when the lazy plan is collected.
N1.label: N1 environment-specific failure established

symptoms_visible: After the Read the Docs job installed Polars 1.8.2, collecting the plan still raised `Series: line, length 1 doesn't match the DataFrame height of 3`.
N2_x.label: N2_x patch-release update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The same length-mismatch exception appears when `POLARS_ALLOW_NON_SCALAR_EXP=1` is configured for the whole Read the Docs runner before the code starts.
N2.label: N2 suppression probe completed

symptoms_visible: With Polars 1.9.0 and the unrelated `sink_parquet()` call removed, collecting the original plan still panics with the same `line` length 1 versus DataFrame height 3 message.
N3_x.label: N3_x minor-release update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The isolated `collect()` still panics with the length-mismatch message when panic and backtrace diagnostics are enabled.
N3.label: N3 fault location captured

symptoms_visible: On the later Polars build, the original `Series: line, length 1 doesn't match the DataFrame height of 3` failure no longer occurs in my rerun.
N_terminal.label: terminal original issue resolved

question_patterns: Can you share the full query or serialize the lazy result immediately before calling `collect()`?
Can you provide the query plan that produces this error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The query is not trivial because it involves multiple functions, but I serialized the lazy result to JSON before `collect()` and shared that full plan. The same plan runs locally; the failure happens 100% of the time while building our documentation on Read the Docs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I reduced it to a direct `select()` where I intentionally return a non-scalar one-element Series alongside a three-row column.
The full serialized plan is the same, but I generated the JSON on a different local Python version.

edges.comment: Reporter c1-c4: the reporter supplied the complete serialized plan and explained that it succeeds locally but consistently fails in the Read the Docs runner. The late `collect()` timing and CI-only behavior were volunteered by the same reporter.

solution.intent: Retry the documentation build after moving from the initially reported release to the next Polars patch release.
solution.concrete_example: Rerun the Read the Docs job after it installs Polars 1.8.2 and check whether the original serialized plan now collects.

edges.comment: Reporter c10: the Read the Docs rerun installed Polars 1.8.2, but the original length-mismatch error remained. This is the same reporter and same documentation deployment.

question_patterns: Set `POLARS_ALLOW_NON_SCALAR_EXP=1` before Polars is imported, rerun the failing job, and report the exact result.
Can you configure the temporary non-scalar-expression environment option for the whole runner and see whether the error is suppressed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first set it immediately before `collect()`, then used the Read the Docs facility to set it for the whole runner before any code starts. I still get the same `Series: line, length 1 doesn't match the DataFrame height of 3` error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the environment variable set before import, the plan collects successfully and the generated data is correct.
Setting it inside Python had no effect, but setting it for the runner before import produced the same original error.

edges.comment: Maintainer c7-c8 and reporter c10-c11: this was a handler-initiated configuration probe that also served as a proposed temporary suppression. The reporter's answer records only where the variable was set and the unchanged exception.

solution.intent: Retry on a newer Polars release while removing the unrelated Parquet sink so the original collection failure can be observed in isolation.
solution.concrete_example: Run the original plan with Polars 1.9.0 after removing `sink_parquet()` and collect it directly.

edges.comment: Reporter c12-c16: the first diagnostic backtrace stopped at a separate `sink_parquet()` failure. The same reporter removed that call and reran on Polars 1.9.0, where the original length mismatch remained.

question_patterns: Set `POLARS_PANIC_ON_ERR=1` and `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` before import, rerun the isolated `collect()`, and paste the full backtrace.
Can you capture a verbose backtrace for the original failure after removing the unrelated sink operation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The panic is still `Series: line, length 1 doesn't match the DataFrame height of 3`. The backtrace includes `polars_mem_engine::executors::projection_utils::check_expand_literals`, then `ProjectionExec::execute_impl`, `ProjectionExec::execute`, and the lazy-frame collect path.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The isolated backtrace never enters projection execution; it fails while deserializing the JSON plan before collection starts.
The same projection and `check_expand_literals` frames appear, with different memory addresses and additional Python frames.

edges.comment: Maintainer c11/c17 and reporter c16: the reporter ran the requested panic/backtrace diagnostics on the isolated original failure. The answer contains raw stack symbols; interpreting them as the fault location is reserved for the final solution's engineer inference.

solution.intent: Treat the original length mismatch as an upstream Polars projection/broadcast-validation defect addressed by the linked upstream change, update to a build containing that correction, remove diagnostic panic settings, and verify the original serialized plan.
solution.concrete_example: Use a later Polars build containing the upstream correction identified by the maintainer, unset the temporary panic diagnostics, and rerun the original three-row serialized query. Confirm that the `line` length mismatch no longer occurs before closing this issue; handle any Parquet, duration, or index-conversion failures separately.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only the serialized plan, repeated runtime outcomes, and raw stack frames. The maintainer inferred that the formatted plan showed no scalar misuse, and the `check_expand_literals` frame localizes the original failure to projection-time literal expansion/broadcast validation. The thread links the fixing upstream change without describing a more precise implementation mechanism, so no deeper root cause should be invented.

edges.comment: Reporter c29-c30 confirmed that the original issue no longer occurred after later reruns; the remaining panic-environment problem was moved to a separate ticket. Maintainer c31 attributed this original issue to a linked upstream fix. The terminal observation is the reporter's own confirmation, while the fix attribution remains maintainer-side.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause at the level established by the thread: an upstream Polars projection/literal-expansion broadcast-validation defect caused the erroneous length-one versus height-three failure; the thread does not establish a more detailed implementation mechanism.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the serialized three-row plan, the CI-only repeated failures, and the backtrace through `check_expand_literals` and projection execution rather than inferred from the exception text alone.
Must not present `POLARS_ALLOW_NON_SCALAR_EXP` or merely moving to the initially tested patch and minor releases as the fix; those in-case attempts still produced the original error.
Must not insist on adding `.first()` as the resolution without demonstrating an actual scalar misuse; the maintainer found no apparent scalar misuse in the formatted query plan.
Must keep the later `sink_parquet()`, duration dictionary-packing, pandas-index conversion, and panic-environment failures separate from this original diagnostic chain.

Must ask the reporter to rerun the original serialized plan on a build containing the upstream correction and only treat this issue as resolved after the reporter confirms the length-mismatch failure is gone.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Python and systems developer; comfortable with serialized lazy plans, CI logs, environment variables, native wheel builds, dynamic-library inspection, Rust backtraces, and reducing failures across execution paths.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, analytical, and cooperative; supplies complete logs and experiments, explicitly distinguishes local behavior from CI behavior, revises hypotheses when new evidence appears, and separates newly discovered failures into other issues.
